findings.description: Removing the guard for request paths starting with '//' lets such a path reach urllib3 unchanged, so the request target can be misparsed as an authority.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a plain-HTTP request whose path begins with a double slash, such as http://example.com//admin, with no proxy. request.path_url is then '//admin', and urllib3 can read it as a network-path reference with host 'admin'. The mechanism is that the removed code prefixed a single slash to avoid this exact misparse. The impact is that the request is sent to the wrong host, possibly leaking credentials or data to an unintended server.
